newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina said to postpone IMF talks until March.
newsitem.headline: Argentina said to postpone IMF talks until March.

text.p: Argentina will postpone its planned talks with the International Monetary Fund on an Extended Fund Facility (EFF) loan for a few months, a top Economy Ministry official said Wednesday.

"The most logical thing to do for now is for us to meet the December and March (standby loan) targets and then start the Extended Fund Facility negotiations," said Carlos Rodriguez, top adviser to Economy Minister Roque Fernandez.

Fernandez had said Argentina would start talks on the EFF before year's end. But Rodriguez told reporters that changes in the current plan accepted by the Fund's board earlier in the day meant talks on the new facility would have to wait.
"Since we have just requested a waiver, it is not common practice to start discussing an extended fund arrangement without first meeting the current standby (targets)," Rodriguez said.

The IMF's executive board earlier in the day approved modifications to Argentina's current $1.2 billion standby loan after the country said it would be unable to meet the targets set when the loan was granted in April.
Argentina requested the waiver in September, asking the IMF to allow it to end 1996 with a budget deficit of about $6.0 billion, up from the originally agreed $2.5 billion deficit.
Rodriguez said the next IMF mission would arrive in December to oversee the country's finances and that future missions would be sent every three months to keep a close watch on the books.

He also reiterated Argentina's economy -- which last year shrank 4.4 percent after three years of an average seven percent growth -- would expand between two and three percent this year and four to five percent in 1997.
After the recent tourmoil, Argentina was counting on a prolonged association with the Fund as a means to reassure investors, Rodriguez said.
"The idea is to get money, which is not a bad thing. But equally important is the institutional support, the Fund's auditing," he said.
